title: Affine coordinate rings have finite Tor dimension from stalkwise finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $Y$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $f:X\to Y$ locally of finite type. Assume every source local ring has finite Tor dimension over its image local ring [def-pc-perfect-morphism]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ and $V\subseteq X$ be affine opens such that $V\subseteq f^{-1}(U)$. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$, with $A\to B$ induced by $f$. There is $d\in\mathbf N$ such that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(B,M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>d$. The empty affine open and the zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 069C, lemma-check-perfect-stalks, proof of (3) implies (1), and the first sentence of (1) implies (2); More on Algebra Tags 068X and 068W; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C

proof.text: Use Mathlib Scheme.Hom.finiteType_appLE on the two affine opens to obtain Algebra.FiniteType A B for the actual coordinate homomorphism. Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial_double_prime gives a surjective polynomial algebra map g. Its commutes equation verifies g composed with C is the coordinate map. Apply affinePolynomial_boundedResolution_of_stalkwise to this presentation.

source.place: Tag 069C, proof of (3) implies (1), finite polynomial presentation

proof.text: Restrict the polynomial projective resolution along C:A->P. Its terms remain flat: polynomial rings are free over A, projective P-modules are flat, and Mathlib Module.Flat.trans gives flatness of each restricted term. Restriction of scalars preserves homology and hence the augmentation quasi-isomorphism; singleMapHomologicalComplex supplies its target identification. restrictScalarsComp_App identifies the augmented target with B restricted along the original coordinate homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 069C, first sentence of (1) implies (2), polynomial-flat restriction

proof.text: For each test module N and j>d, tensoring the zero degree-j term gives a zero term. ExactAt.of_isZero and ExactAt.isZero_homology give vanishing homology. flatResolution_torComparison transports this vanishing to Tor_prime for the doubly restricted B. The scalar-restriction composition isomorphism, mapped by Tor_prime, transports it to the target Tor object.

lean.statement:
theorem affineSections_finiteTorDimension_of_stalkwise
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hperfect : HasStalkwiseFiniteTorDimension f)
    (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U), ∀ j : ℕ, d < j →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U)) j).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.appLE U V e).hom).obj
          (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, V) Γ(X, V)))).obj M)
